texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident that occurred on 18.01.2020, in which one Bhoop Singh (aged about 41) allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 18.01.2020 at 7:30 a.m. victim Bhoop Singh along with passengers Seema, Usha, Ruby, Priti, Priyanka and minor children Adarsh@Arjun, Gurpreet and Shahil were returning to Delhi from Aligarh after attending a marriage function. All of them were travelling in an Ecco car bearing no.DL-3CCR-1409, which was being driven by petitioner Bhoop Singh. When they reached Chand Hut chowk, Palwal, a truck bearing no.HR-55G-7560 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle), came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco Car. Due to the impact, all the passengers, including the driver/petitioner sustained severe injuries. Victims including Bhoop Singh were rushed to Civil hospital at Palwal. His MLC was prepared. 3. An FIR No.0018/2020, dated 18.01.2020, u/s 279/304-A/337 IPC was registered at PS Chand Hut, District Palwal. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/337/338/304A IPC before concerned criminal court. Present claim petition has been filed in respect of injured Bhoop Singh while separate claim petitions were filed before this Tribunal for compensation claim in respect of victim Ruby vide case titled as Ashutosh Dixit vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.225/20, victim Priti Charu by Charu gupta gupta 17:57:24 +0530 MACT No:120/21 Bhoop Singh vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 2 of 22 BK vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.123/21, Priyanka vide case titled as Priyanka Devi v. Sant Prakash, MACT no.121/21, minor Adarsh @ Arjun through his mother Priti vide case titled as Adarsh vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.124/21, Usha vide case titled as Usha v. Sant Prakash, MACT no.125/21, minor Gurpreet (since deceased) vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.118/21, minor Sahil (since deceased) vide case titled as Seema Devi v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.122/21 and Seema Devi, vide case titled as Seema Devi v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.119/21. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3. 5. In response to the claim petition, respondent no.1 and 2 filed their written statement/reply without denying the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle or allegations or rash and negligent driving. It has been pleaded that Respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle possessed a valid driving licence at the time of accident, that the vehicle was duly insured, that the vehicle was fit to ply on the road and had requisite fitness and permit issued vide Form No.47, NPPUC. 6. A written statement/reply was filed by respondent no.3 denying its liability to compensate the petitioner in case respondent no.1 and 2 were found to be in breach of the terms of the insurance policy. Insurance company has further raised a plea of contributory negligence on the part of victims Bhoop Singh vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28723701/ 2 in as much as the Ecco Car was being plied in violation of the permit, beyond its seating capacity of 7 persons. It is pleaded that the Ecco car admittedly carried 12 signed Digitally Charu by Charu gupta Date: MACT No:120/21 Bhoop Singh vs.Sant Prakash & ors. gupta 2025.12.17 17:57:28 +0530 P.No. 3 of 22 BK passengers including the driver and must have met the accident owing to disbalance. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 19.02.2022. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 18.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-55G-7560 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 8. In order to prove her claim, petitioner/injured examined himself as PW-1. To prove his claim, petitioner /Bhoop Singh led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he deposed that on 08.01.2020 at about 7:30 a.m. injured was returning to his house from Aligarh, U.P after attending a marriage function by an Ecco car bearing no.DL3CCR1409 along with Ruby, Seema, Priti, Usha, Priyanka, Pinki Devi and children namely Gurpreet,Shahil and Adarsh. When they reached Chand Hut chowk at village Chandhut Palwal, Haryana, a vehicle bearing no.HR-55G-7560, came from opposite directions in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco car. Due to sudden and forceful impact, injured sustained several grievous injuries. Victim was moved to Civil Hospital, Palwal, Haryana where doctors referred him to Safdarjung Hospital. He was medically examined. PW-1 relied upon his Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/1, MLC as Ex.PW1/2, discharge summary as Ex.PW1/3, OPD cards as Ex.PW1/4, Medical bills and records as Ex.PW1/5 & Digitally signed Charu by Charu gupta Date: gupta 2025.12.17 17:57:37 +0530 MACT No:120/21 Bhoop Singh vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 4 of 22 BK Bhoop Singh vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28723701/ 3 Ex.PW-1/5A, DAR i.e. FIR, chargesheet, arrest memo, site plan, mechanical inspection as Ex.PW1/6 and DL as Ex.PW-1/7. PW-1 was cross - examined by all respondents. Ms. Priyanka/PW-2 was examined as an eye witness. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She deposed that she was witness in all the 9 cases and injured in case titled as Priyanka vs. Sant Prakash. She relied upon her Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1, copy of her MLC as Ex.PW1/2, her OPD card as Ex.PW1/3, her medical bills as Ex.PW1/4 and complete criminal record as Ex.PW1/5. She was cross examined by learned counsel for insurance company and the same was adopted by Respondents did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. As already discussed, principal award amount/ compensation will be payable by the insurance company with simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of petition till actual realization. Insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the award amount in favour of the petitioner with State Bank of India, District Court Complex, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT PARKING FUND, A/c No. 00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner.

P.No. 5 of 22 BK 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. P.No. 6 of 22 BK a deduction of at least 50% is liable Bhoop Singh vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28723701/ 4 to be made on account of contributory negligence. Even if four minor passengers allegedly travelling in the said car are ignored to have caused overloading or excess weight, the presence of other nine adult passengers (including the driver) in the car would still be considered as a traffic violation. However, before such traffic violation can be equated to contributory negligence, the concept of contributory negligence may be analysed through the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramod kumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kungvargi Tak and Ors.,C.A. No.5436 of 1994 decided on 05.08.2002, wherein it has been held as under: "...9. Subject to non-requirement of the existence of duty, the question of contributory negligence is to be decided on the same principle on which the question of defendant's negligence is decided. The standard of reasonable man is as relevant in the case of plaintiff's contributory negligence as in the case of defendant's negligence. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi-gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so , to what degree. Contribu-tory negligence Charu by Charu gupta MACT No:120/21 P.No. 7 of 22 BK 17:57:54 +0530 focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." Bhoop Singh vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28723701/ 5 13. Reliance also placed on recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd. Siddiqui vs. National Insurance Co. (2020) 3SCC 57 wherein the court while considering an issue of triple riding made following observations: " a pillion rider, even if accompanied by more than legally permitted number of passengers, does not automatically imply contributory negligence. For such a finding, it must be demonstrated that the pillion rider's action directly contributed to the occurrence of the accident or exacerbated its impact. The court emphasised that a violation of traffic laws such as exceeding the permissible number of riders on a motorcycle, does not by itself establish contributory negligence. There must be a clear causal connection between the violation and the accident". 17:58:06 +0530 MACT No:120/21 Bhoop Singh vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 8 of 22 BK It is argued that such admission leads to an inference that the petitioner, who was also driving the Ecco car, must have fallen asleep during driving, thereby leading to accident. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam Insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an Bhoop Singh vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28723701/ 6 adverse inference can be drawn against him. 19. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 20.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 20.7. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 7.5% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to MACT No:120/21 Bhoop Singh vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 18 of 22 BK invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
